evaluations.label: A
errors: Says the industrial designer alone is to produce the final banana-form design and the UI designer to finalize layout; the project manager only asked for the final look and feel and UI design, with both designers working together on the prototype.
Describes a 'hard internal structure' and 'Backlit buttons confirmed' more firmly than the transcript supports; the light trigger was left unresolved and the structure was only loosely discussed.

Frames the plastic cover as reconsidered with a 'recess or offset' alternative; the UI designer only suggested placing the channel numbers somewhere out of the way, and the project manager just said okay.
strengths: Accurate recap of the previous meeting's decisions.
Correctly captures the retained wheel with the 50x cost and the 12 euro limit, banana and yellow, spongy cover, standard battery and chip-on-print.
Voice recognition chip correctly recorded as deferred.
Clear next steps: final look and feel, UI design, joint prototype work, evaluation against user requirements.
Notes the left/right hand discussion and the battery concern for always-on light.
weaknesses: Omits that further instructions will arrive by email.
Next steps assign work to individual roles more specifically than the transcript did.
Does not name who raised each point, so it has little on who said what.

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'IS1001c remote control' does not appear anywhere in the transcript.
Uses the label 'UIZ' for the user interface designer, which is not in the transcript, and an outline that uses 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' inconsistent with the roles.
Says backlit buttons 'activate upon movement'; the trigger was debated (motion versus on-press) and never decided.
Action Items section says '(none)' although the project manager asked for final look and feel, the UI design, evaluation, and joint prototype work by both designers.
'Arched internal structure for component mounting' is an overstated paraphrase of the casing discussion.
strengths: Good coverage of the cost issue, the wheel decision, the plastic cover objection, the banana and spongy decision.
Useful unresolved-questions list (voice chip, motion sensor cost against the 12 euro limit, spongy material against button presses).
The outline follows the order of the meeting.
weaknesses: No action items despite clear next steps (the next steps are only in the outline).
Redundant structure (summary plus outline) with confusing speaker labels.
Does not mention emailed instructions or the left/right-hand discussion.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Says the earlier concept had a 'preview button'; the transcript says previous channel button.
Says the wheel could be pressed down 'to recall a channel'; the user interface designer said the push-down could be used for the record function.
Several timestamps do not match the content (for example the 04:48 voice chip citation sits after the 04:11 cost point but the 06:14 and 11:04 citations do not correspond to the cited statements).

Says the group 'asked the industrial and UI designers to develop it together' with the chip 'selected', which is fine, but the lead summary calls the wheel a 'possible differentiator' while the group definitively kept it.
strengths: Detailed and mostly accurate on the voice chip, the continuous-light battery concern, the cover objection, the pear versus banana debate, and the yellow company color.
Honestly states that the left/right-hand concern had no documented resolution.
Mentions further instructions by email and the evaluation of the product against requirements.
weaknesses: The Action items heading is empty, and the tasks are only in the body text.
Heavy timestamp use with some wrong citations.
Structure scatters the decisions across sections, so a reader needs effort to find what was decided.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested' is not in the transcript; the project manager said an odd-shaped structure with a spongy cover.
Calls the UI designer 'UL Hazred', a garbled version of the name.
Action item 'Assess cost implications of wheel sensor' for the industrial designer was never assigned.
Action item 'Develop banana-shaped spongy case design' for the industrial designer alone and 'Finalize UI design' tied to a timestamp of 18:42 are not assignments made in the meeting.
'Provide meeting notes in shared folder' mischaracterizes the project manager saying he would take notes.
Lists the banana as 'proposed' rather than decided and does not record the standard battery or chip-on-print decision.
strengths: Only set of notes with an owner-by-owner action list, including the project manager's email instructions and the joint prototype work.
Records the symmetry for left/right hands and the lighted buttons to identify the side.
Records the priority of fancy look over function and yellow matching the company color.
weaknesses: Omits the voice recognition chip, the battery and chip details, and the 12 euro discussion's resolution.
Several invented or inflated action items reduce trust.
Thin on the final concept decision (wheel on top, buttons on side, spongy cover over odd shape).

rationale: A is the most accurate and gives the clearest account of what was decided, what was deferred and what comes next, with only mild over-assignment of tasks. C is detailed and mostly sound, but has a few wrong details (preview button, push-down used to recall a channel), poor timestamps and an empty action items section. B covers the content well and has a good unresolved-questions list, but it invents a product code and a speaker label, wrongly says the backlight trigger was decided, and lists no action items. D is the only one with owner-labeled actions, but several are unsupported, it invents a heart-shaped core, garbles a name, and omits the voice chip and battery decisions.
